summary: Checks whether a value is **not** a URL.
description: `nonUrl(value)` is the same test as `!isUrl(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.
An `http`, `https` or `ftp` URL with something after the scheme and no whitespace anywhere. A bare host such as `"example.com"` is not one.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is not a URL; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
nonUrl("example.com"); // => true
nonUrl("https://"); // => true
nonUrl("https://exa mple.com"); // => true
nonUrl("https://example.com"); // => false
nonUrl("http://example.com/a?b=1"); // => false
```
